rules.title: Secrets in env or vault
rules.text: Load secrets from environment variables or a secret manager; never hardcode them.

rules.title: Prevent injection
rules.text: Use parameterized queries and safe APIs; never build SQL, shell commands or HTML by string concatenation with user input.

rules.title: Check authorization server-side
rules.text: Enforce authentication and authorization on the server for every protected operation.

rules.title: Vet dependencies
rules.text: Pin dependency versions, commit lockfiles and review new packages before adding them.

rules.title: Least privilege
rules.text: Grant the minimum permissions needed for tokens, service accounts and containers.

rules.title: Use vetted crypto
rules.text: Use well-reviewed cryptographic libraries; never invent your own algorithms or store plain passwords.

rules.title: Follow OWASP guidance
rules.text: Follow OWASP Top 10 and ASVS guidance when handling web input, sessions and authentication.

rules.title: Output encoding
rules.text: Encode output for its context and avoid injecting raw HTML; sanitize rich text with a vetted library.

rules.title: CSRF protection
rules.text: Protect state-changing browser requests with CSRF tokens or SameSite cookies.

rules.title: Strict CORS
rules.text: Configure CORS with explicit origins; never reflect arbitrary origins with credentials.

rules.title: Security headers
rules.text: Set security headers such as Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options and Strict-Transport-Security.

rules.title: Safe sessions
rules.text: Use HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies and rotate session identifiers on login.

rules.title: Guard outbound requests
rules.text: Validate and allow-list URLs before fetching user-supplied addresses to prevent SSRF.

rules.title: Safe file uploads
rules.text: Validate uploads: allow-list extensions, check the real file type instead of the Content-Type header, set a size limit and store files outside the web root.

rules.title: Password hashing
rules.text: Hash passwords with Argon2id, or scrypt or bcrypt where it is unavailable, with a unique salt; never use fast hashes such as SHA-256.

rules.title: Constant-time comparison
rules.text: Compare secrets and tokens in constant time.

rules.title: Secret scanning
rules.text: Run secret scanning in CI and rotate any credential that has been exposed.
